    Important Words
    • īśvaraḥ — the controller, Supersoul
      From √īś, 'to rule.' Gauḍīya frame: īśvara is Bhagavān as the controller of all jīvas and prakṛti. The verse names Him as īśvara of the body, senses, and life of every being — Paramātmā in His full Vaiṣṇava sense.
    • kālaḥ — the time factor
      From √kal, 'to count, drive.' Kṛṣṇa identifies Himself as kāla in Gītā 10.30 and 11.32. Gauḍīya: kāla is His agency of change — what creates, sustains, and destroys is His own time-form, not an impersonal force.
    • viṣṇuḥ — all-pervading
      From √viś, 'to enter, pervade.' Viṣṇu is Kṛṣṇa's aiśvarya-aspect, the all-pervading Lord. The verse identifies Kṛṣṇa-the-toddler with Viṣṇu-the-pervasive — Gauḍīya siddhānta: Kṛṣṇa is the source, Viṣṇu the plenary expansion.
    • prakṛtiḥ — the cosmic manifestation
      From pra-√kṛ, 'to bring forth.' Kṛṣṇa is named as prakṛti also — not external to His own material energy. Gauḍīya: prakṛti is His parā or aparā śakti, never a rival principle; here He is identified as her substrate.
    • rajaḥ-sattva-tamaḥ-mayī — consisting of the three modes
      Compound: rajas + sattva + tamas + mayī (made of). Prakṛti is the three-guṇa fabric. Gauḍīya: bhakti is nirguṇa — it operates outside this three-mode weave even while the practitioner has a guṇa-body.
    • vikāra-vit — knower of the restless mind
      Compound: vikāra (modification) + vit (knower). Paramātmā knows every flicker of the heart's modifications. Gauḍīya: this is the basis for nāma-aparādha doctrine — Kṛṣṇa sees the intention behind every chant.
    You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the controller of everything. The body, life, ego and senses of every living entity are Your own self. You are the Supreme Person, Viṣṇu, the imperishable controller. You are the time factor, the immediate cause, and You are material nature, consisting of the three modes passion, goodness and ignorance. You are the original cause of this material manifestation. You are the Supersoul, and therefore You know everything within the core of the heart of every living entity.
    Purport

    Śrīpāda Madhvācārya has quoted from the Vāmana Purāṇa as follows: rūpyatvāt tu jagad rūpaṁ viṣṇoḥ sākṣāt sukhātmakam nitya-pūrṇaṁ samuddiṣṭaṁ svarūpaṁ paramātmanaḥ

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the controller of everything. The body, life, ego and senses of every living entity are Your own self. You are the Supreme Person, Viṣṇu, the imperishable controller. You are the time factor, the immediate cause, and You are material nature, consisting of the three modes passion, goodness and ignorance. You are the original cause of this material manifestation. You are the Supersoul, and therefore You know everything within the core of the heart of every living entity.
    Commentary

    "No one except you is the cause of bondage. You are the Lord of all because everything is one with you. You are thus the lord of the body, the pranas (asu) the ahankara (atma). You are time, for time is your effect, your action. You are prakrtih, because prakrti is your sakti. You are also the paramatma (adhyaksa). You know everything including the minds (vikaran) of all bodies. Therefore the one bhagavan, Visnu, isvara, is you."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The meaning of the first line is as follows. We are worthy of your mercy because we are devoid of offense, since you are the inspiration behind all actions and because you are naturally the sole controller internally and externally. (You have done everything.) “Time is the instigator of all actions. Mahat-tattva and other elements are the cause of the universe. This is what some say.” The second line answers. As time, the cause, you are Bhāgavān—having all abilities. You are viṣṇu—spreading everywhere and you are avyaya—without destructions. You are īśvara—controlling everything. You, possessing all its qualities, are the main time, since time is your aṁśa. Though mahat-tattva spreads everywhere, you are the chief mahān since you are the cause of mahat-tattva pervading everywhere. In the Third Canto it is said: bhagavān eka āsedam agra ātmātmanāṁ vibhuḥ ātmecchānugatāv ātmā nānā-maty-upalakṣaṇaḥ Bhagavān, who exists in the form of Paramātmā and Brahman, alone existed before the creation of the universe, when the desire to create bodies of the jīvas was absent. SB 3.5.23 As Bhagavān, you are the chief prakṛti because you are unchanging as the final cause. You are the chief puruṣa, since you are the lord of the body and senses, since the other puruṣa is your aṁśa. You are the subtle cause (sūkṣmāḥ) of prakṛti composed of the eight elements mentioned in Bhagavad-gītā. Distinct from your sac-cid-ānanda-śakti, you are qualified with the three guṇas in the universe. Because prakṛti obeys your temperament, it is called prakṛti. You are mūla-prakṛti according to the statement of Brahma-sūtra (1.4.23) pratijṣā-dṛṣtāntānurodhāt: the Lord is the material cause, since the view is not in opposition to the scriptures. Or sūkṣmāḥ means prakṛti which is difficult to understand. “Am I composed of the guṇas?” No, you are devoid of rajas, sattva or tama (arajas-sattva-tammayī). You are avyakta because you have subtle conscious form. Instead of avyakta sometimes adhyākṣaḥ is seen. You are the controller of the body and senses. This is further described: you investigate all the changes of the bodies (kṣetra). nātmā jajāna na mariṣyati naidhate 'sau na kṣīyate savana-vid vyabhicāriṇāṁ hi sarvatra śaśvad anapāyy upalabdhi-mātraṁ prāṇo yathendriya-balena vikalpitaṁ sat The ātmā does not undergo birth, death, growth, or deterioration since he is the seer of all conditions of changing bodies. That ātmā is knowledge alone, existing constantly in the body, but endowed with activity by the power of the senses, just as prāṇa is one but moves from body to body. SB 11.3.38 Or the meaning of the last line can be “you are the puruṣa, cause of creation of prakṛti, beyond all perceptions. Another version has sarva-sākṣī.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The meaning of the first line is as follows. We are worthy of your mercy because we are devoid of offense, since you are the inspiration behind all actions and because you are naturally the sole controller internally and externally. (You have done everything.) “Time is the instigator of all actions. Mahat-tattva and other elements are the cause of the universe. This is what some say.” The second line answers. As time, the cause, you are Bhāgavān—having all abilities. You are viṣṇu—spreading everywhere and you are avyaya—without destruction. You are īśvara—controlling everything. You, possessing all its qualities, are the main time, since time is your aṁśa. You become the guṇas, in order to create variety in the world, but this is separate from your śakti of eternity, knowledge and bliss. Or the guṇas refers to the jīva being covered (puruṣaḥ). You are avyaktaḥ (instead of adhyakṣaḥ), because as pure consciousness you are very subtle. You are the ruler of the body (adhyakṣaḥ). This is then described: you know about all the changes of the bodies. nātmā jajāna na mariṣyati naidhate 'sau na kṣīyate savana-vid vyabhicāriṇāṁ hi The jīva does not undergo birth, death, growth, or deterioration since he is the seer of all conditions of changing bodies. SB 11.3.38 Or adhyakṣaḥ refers to the controller of prakṛti. The Lord witnesses prakṛti for creation. Or time, prakṛti, the jīva and the Lord are listed in sequence of superiority in regards to creation.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa alone is the kāla, prakṛti, and puruṣa within every heart — surrender to Him is surrender to the One already running everything.
    Practical Applications
    • Before any decision today, pause and acknowledge that Kṛṣṇa as Paramātmā already knows your motive — speak and act accordingly.
    • Notice when you credit 'time' or 'circumstances' for an outcome, and re-attribute it consciously to Kṛṣṇa as kāla and īśvara.
    • Refuse to treat the three guṇas as 'just my personality' — name the mode operating in you right now (sattva, rajas, or tamas) and offer it to Him.
    Analogy

    A puppet-master holds every string — strings of breath, mind, senses, time, and the very stage on which the play unfolds. The puppets argue over which of them is acting, while He alone moves the limbs. Kṛṣṇa as Paramātmā, as kāla, as prakṛti, as puruṣa, is the single hand behind every movement of every body.

    Important Words
    • agrāhyaḥ — not confined in a material body
      From a- (not) + √grah, 'to grasp.' Kṛṣṇa is not grasp-able — by sense, by mind, by argument. Gauḍīya: agrāhya is the negative pole; sevonmukha (service-faced) is the positive correlate that makes the agrāhya graspable.
    • vikāraiḥ — by agitations (of the mind)
      Instrumental plural of vikāra — same root as vikāra-vit (SB 10.10.31). The mind's modifications are now named as the very reason the mind cannot know Kṛṣṇa. The same organ that He knows fully cannot know Him.
    • prākṛtaiḥ — by material
      Adjective from prakṛti. The qualities are 'of prakṛti' — material. Gauḍīya distinction: prākṛta-guṇas (material modes) vs. aprākṛta-guṇas (Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities). They cannot reach across the gap.
    • prāk-siddham — established before (creation)
      Compound: prāk (before) + siddha (established). Kṛṣṇa existed prior to the material manifestation. Gauḍīya: He is nitya — anādi (without beginning) and ananta (without end). The verse's verb is not 'created'; it is 'existed already.'
    • guṇa-saṁvṛtaḥ — covered by the modes
      Compound: guṇa + saṁvṛta (covered). The investigator's body is itself the veil. The verse diagnoses: the very faculty trying to know Him is what blocks the knowing. Solution: change the faculty's direction (sevā), not its sharpness (study).
    O Lord, You exist before the creation. Therefore, who, trapped by a body of material qualities in this material world, can understand You?
    Purport

    As it is said: ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ ( Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu 1.2.234) Kṛṣṇa’s name, attributes and form are Absolute Truth, existing before the creation. Therefore, how can those who are created — that is, those entrapped in bodies created of material elements — understand Kṛṣṇa perfectly? This is not possible. But, sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ: Kṛṣṇa reveals Himself to those engaged in devotional service. This is also confirmed in Bhagavad-gītā (18.55) by the Lord Himself: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti. Even the descriptions of Kṛṣṇa in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam are sometimes misunderstood by less intelligent men with a poor fund of knowledge. Therefore, the best course by which to know Him is to engage oneself in pure devotional activities. The more one advances in devotional activities, the more one can understand Him as He is. If from the material platform one could understand Kṛṣṇa, then, since Kṛṣṇa is everything ( sarvaṁ khalv idaṁ brahma ), one could understand Kṛṣṇa by seeing anything within this material world. But that is not possible. mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ ( Bg. 9.4 ) Everything is resting on Kṛṣṇa, and everything is Kṛṣṇa, but this is not to be realized by persons on the material platform.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Lord, You exist before the creation. Therefore, who, trapped by a body of material qualities in this material world, can understand You?
    Commentary

    Only by your mercy can you be seen. Practically, you are invisible. You are not perceivable by the intelligence and senses (vikaraih) which are observed by you (grhyamanaih). Why? Because they arise from the modes of nature(prakrtair guna). If you are non-material, then can the jiva perceive or know you? No, no one in this world can know you (ko’nv iha), who are the cause of the jiva (praksiddham), if he is covered by the modes (gunavrtah). However the devotee, who is beyond the modes, can know you to some extent through bhakti.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Who can directly meet you (vijṣātum arhati)? You are not grasped by the transformations of intelligence (prakṛtaiḥ vikāraiḥ) or the senses (guṇaiḥ). Even though you are merciful and appear directly before us, we cannot understand you in truth or control you. You cannot be controlled by those who directly realize you (gṛhyamānaiḥ), who are devoid of transformations (avikāraiḥ), who are endowed with natural qualities like mercy, because you are completely independent. Taking the other meaning, you cannot be understood in truth since you are beyond intellect, since you are one, but have simultaneously a most powerful form and a human form. What person, taking complete shelter (saṁvṛtaḥ) of the qualities of bhakti (guṇa), can know in detail about you, even though you are eternally present (prak-siddham) in Nanda-gokula. Who is qualified? No one is able to know you since your pastimes are most difficult to understand both on earth and in the spiritual realm. Or, though you cannot be tied by ropes (guṇaiḥ), you have become bound by them (guṇa- samśṛitaḥ). Another version has saṁvṛtaḥ—completely covered. Out of respect they do not mention who bound him. Seeing him bound up, they become completely bewildered and thus utter, “Who indeed can understand?”

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa exists before creation and beyond material guṇas; only through sevā does He reveal Himself — surrender the speculator, take up service.
    Practical Applications
    • Refuse to 'figure out' Kṛṣṇa today through argument or theory; instead, offer one concrete act of sevā (chanting, cooking for the Deity, serving a Vaiṣṇava) and let realization come through the tongue and hands.
    • Notice when your guṇa-conditioned mind reduces Kṛṣṇa to a concept, symbol, or 'energy' — pause, and re-affirm: He is the prākṛta-guṇa-atīta Personality who existed before this body and these moods.
    • Before opening Bhāgavatam or Gītā today, speak aloud the prayer 'sevonmukhe hi jihvādau' — read not to master the text but to be revealed to by it.
    Analogy

    A man inside a sealed clay pot, looking out through cracks, tries to describe the potter. He sees clay, hears the wheel, feels the wet finger — but the potter Himself is on the other side of the wall. Bound in a guṇa-body, the conditioned soul has no organ to grasp Kṛṣṇa who existed before any pot was thrown. Only sevā breaks the wall.

    Stories
    Rūpa Gosvāmī's instruction on sevonmukha

    Rūpa Gosvāmī, in Padyāvalī and Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, formulates the verse: ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ / sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ — Kṛṣṇa's name, form, qualities, pastimes cannot be grasped by the material senses; only when the senses turn toward service does He spontaneously reveal Himself.

    SB 10.10.32 is the scriptural seed Rūpa is unfolding. The siddhas concede that no guṇa-bound being can understand Kṛṣṇa by speculation — the chapter has just demonstrated the only path: His own descent into their captivity, His own breaking of the trees. Revelation, not investigation.

    Important Words
    • vāsudevāya — to Vāsudeva, the origin of the caturvyūha
      Dative of Vāsudeva. Gauḍīya pañcatattva of Vāsudeva-Saṅkarṣaṇa-Pradyumna-Aniruddha: Vāsudeva is the first of the caturvyūha, source of the other three. The toddler is addressed by His highest aiśvarya-name.
    • vedhase — to the origin of creation
      Dative of Vedhas — 'arranger.' An epithet usually applied to Brahmā; here applied to Kṛṣṇa as the source of the very arranger. Gauḍīya: even Brahmā's creative power is Kṛṣṇa's borrowed potency (śakti).
    • ātma-dyota-guṇaiḥ-channa-mahimne — whose glories are veiled by His own energies
      Compound: ātma (own) + dyota (effulgence) + guṇaiḥ (by qualities) + channa (covered) + mahimne (to the one of glory). Gauḍīya: yogamāyā veils the Lord's full aiśvarya in Vraja so that mādhurya can play. The veil is the līlā's enabler.
    • brahmaṇe — to the Supreme Brahman
      Dative of Brahman. Gauḍīya: Bhagavān is the source of Brahman (brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham, Gītā 14.27). The verse identifies Kṛṣṇa as the substrate of impersonal Brahman, not its derivative — explicitly inverting the Advaitin reading.
    • namaḥ — respectful obeisances
      Indeclinable. The whole verse ends in namaḥ — analysis surrenders to bow. Gauḍīya tradition's parikrama of every philosophical inquiry ends in namaḥ; jñāna terminates in bhakti, not the other way around.
    O Lord, whose glories are covered by Your own energy, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. You are Saṅkarṣaṇa, the origin of creation, and You are Vāsudeva, the origin of the caturvyūha. Because You are everything and are therefore the Supreme Brahman, we simply offer our respectful obeisances unto You.
    Purport

    Instead of trying to understand Kṛṣṇa in detail, it is better to offer our respectful obeisances unto Him, for He is the origin of everything and He is everything. Because we are covered by the material modes of nature, He is very difficult for us to understand unless He reveals Himself to us. Therefore it is better for us to acknowledge that He is everything and offer obeisances unto His lotus feet.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Lord, whose glories are covered by Your own energy, You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead. You are Saṅkarṣaṇa, the origin of creation, and You are Vāsudeva, the origin of the caturvyūha. Because You are everything and are therefore the Supreme Brahman, we simply offer our respectful obeisances unto You.
    Commentary

    Because you are difficult to know, we simply offer our respects to you. That is the intention of this verse. We offer respects to you, the creator of the universe (vedhase). Why are you hard to know? Because of the covering of the gunas. This is made clearer. As the sun is covered by clouds (created by the sun) your glory is covered by the gunas which are created by you (atma dyota).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    We offer respects to you, unto he who is famous as Svayam Bhagavān (tasmai), who is also known as Mahā-vakuṇṭha-nātha or Nārāyaṇa (bhagavate), to the first member of the catur-vyūha (vāsudevāya), to the creator taking the puruṣa forms like Saṅkarṣaṇa (vedhase), the forms whose greatness is covered by your personal qualities, and covered by the impersonal manifestation Brahman for persons qualified for it. Or brahmane can mean a summarization of the previous forms: “unto the greatest, who contains everything else.” The meaning also indicates forms according to his pastimes. We offer respect to that person with an eternally perfect form in Nanda-gokula (tasmai), to you, the son of Nanda (tubhyam), to Bhagavān. We offer respects to you who sometimes become the son of Vasudeva, who produce most astonishing pastimes (vedhase), who cover your powers with your childhood pastimes endowed with self-revealing qualities (ātmā-dyotaiḥ guṇaiḥ) , or to you who cover your powers by being bound by ropes shining with your effulgence. We offer respects to you, in whom everything becomes possible (brahmaṇe).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    We offer respects to the supreme Lord (bhagavate), the deity of citta (vāsudevāya), the creator of the universe (vedhase), who spreads throughout the universe (brahmane). Or we offer respects to the lord endowed with six qualities (bhagavate), who appeared from Vasudeva to display those qualities, (vāsudevāya), to give benefit to all jīvas (vedhase), who is thus the greatest of all, not covered by anything (brahmane). You cover your greatness by the power of qualities emanating from you. Or we offer respects to the son of Vasudeva, most difficult to understand because you are also endowed with all powers (bhagavate). You thus reveal your nature as Bhagavān by astonishing pastimes as the creator (vedhase). You are the greatest (mahimne), unlimited, the opposite of being small but that is hidden by being bound up with ropes (guṇa). Still you are spread everywhere (brahmane). You are unlimited but limited by ropes. How is it possible to bind a waist of eternity, knowledge and bliss by material ropes? The ropes are self-manifesting (ātmadyotaiḥ), made of eternity, knowledge and bliss.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's full glory is veiled by His own energy — stop trying to dissect Him; bow and offer obeisances at His lotus feet today.
    Practical Applications
    • Before study or work today, offer praṇāma to Kṛṣṇa with the explicit acknowledgment, 'You are the origin of everything; I am covered by the modes.'
    • Notice when you are intellectually 'cracking open' Kṛṣṇa to satisfy your mind — pause, and substitute a humble obeisance in place of that analysis.
    • Refuse the impersonalist habit of reducing Him to 'consciousness' or 'the Absolute'; address Him by name as Vāsudeva when you pray today.
    Analogy

    The sun's own brilliance hides the sun from the naked eye — try to stare, and you only see the dazzle. Kṛṣṇa's own ātma-dyota-guṇas (His personal energies) cover His full glory; the seer is dazzled by the very effulgence he hoped would reveal the source. Only when He withdraws a fold of His energy can the surrendered soul see Him plainly.

    You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the master of all auspiciousness .
    Important Words
    • avatārāḥ — incarnations
      Nominative plural of avatāra — 'descent.' Not 'birth' or 'emergence' but descent from the eternal Vaikuṇṭha plane. Gauḍīya frame: avatāras are vibhinnāṁśa-rūpas of Bhagavān, not creations or emanations in the Brahmā sense.
    • aśarīriṇaḥ — not in material bodies
      Genitive of a-śarīrin — 'one without a (material) body.' The whole impersonalist reading (that the avatāra is a temporary māyā-form) is refused by this single word. The form is His own person, not a contingent prakṛti-product.
    • atulya — incomparable
      From a- (not) + tulya (equal). The deeds of the avatāra cannot be matched by any creature of the same nominal species — no fish lifts the Vedas, no boar lifts the earth. The qualifier protects the reader from the literalist reduction.
    • bhavāya — for the elevation
      Dative of bhava — used here in the sense of 'becoming, flourishing.' The avatāra descends for the spiritual elevation of all beings. Paired with vibhavāya (liberation) — material existence is to be turned toward Bhagavān, then transcended.
    • aṁśa-bhāgena — in full potency
      Compound: aṁśa (part) + bhāga (portion). Gauḍīya tattva distinguishes aṁśa-avatāras and pūrṇa-avatāras. Read with the surrounding verses (which name Vāsudeva, the original), this refers to the avatāra's coming in full plenary potency — not a fraction.
    Appearing in bodies like those of an ordinary fish, tortoise and hog, You exhibit activities impossible for such creatures to perform — extraordinary, incomparable, transcendental activities of unlimited power and strength. These bodies of Yours, therefore, are not made of material elements, but are incarnations of Your Supreme Personality. You are the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, who have now appeared, with full potency, for the benefit of all living entities within this material world.
    Purport

    As stated in Bhagavad-gītā (4.7-8): yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge Kṛṣṇa appears as an incarnation when real spiritual life declines and when rogues and thieves increase to disturb the situation of the world. Unfortunate, less intelligent persons, bereft of devotional service, cannot understand the Lord’s activities, and therefore such persons describe these activities as kalpanā — mythology or imagination — because they are rascals and the lowest of men ( na māṁ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ ). Such men cannot understand that the events described by Vyāsadeva in the Purāṇas and other śāstras are not fictitious or imaginary, but factual. Kṛṣṇa, in His full, unlimited potency, here shows that He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for although the two trees were so large and sturdy that even many elephants could not move them, Kṛṣṇa, as a child, exhibited such extraordinary strength that they fell down with a great sound. From the very beginning, by killing Pūtanā, Śakaṭāsura and Tṛṇāvartāsura, by causing the trees to fall, and by showing the entire universe within His mouth, Kṛṣṇa proved that He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The lowest of men ( mūḍhas ), because of sinful activities, cannot understand this, but devotees can accept it without a doubt. Thus the position of a devotee is different from that of a nondevotee.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Appearing in bodies like those of an ordinary fish, tortoise and hog, You exhibit activities impossible for such creatures to perform—extraordinary, incomparable, transcendental activities of unlimited power and strength. These bodies of Yours, therefore, are not made of material elements, but are incarnations of Your Supreme Personality. You are the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, who have now appeared, with full potency, for the benefit of all living entities within this material world.
    Commentary

    "Yes, I am the supreme Lord, but by what characteristics do you discern me as the supreme?" Their answer is given in this verse. "Though having no material body (asarininah) You can be known (jnayate) through the remarkable exploits (viryaih) in various forms like fish and turtle. You ( sa bhavan) are the avatari, source of all avataras, because you with a small drop of your strength as a sporting baby, uprooted trees as strong as Arjuna, which a thousand hands cannot uproot, and because you gave supernatural strength to the rope and the mortar also. You, the giver of all desires (asisam patih), have appeared for the fortune and liberation (bhavaya vibhavaya) of all, with parts of your parts ( amsa bhagena) such as Siva and Brahma".

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    They express their sentiments for the Lord. Though do not have a material body (aśarīriṇaḥ), your avatāras can be inferred in various bodies like Matsya. Or though the avatāras have bodies, those bodies do not have the qualities of material bodies (aśarīriṇaḥ). Another version has śarīriṣu, with the same meaning. They are inferred by their indescribable powers or astonishing activities (atulyātiśayaiḥ vīryaiḥ), which are not found in material bodies. Since the avatāras can be identified by their qualities, what to speak of identifying the avatarī? Or, the two speak after saying “You make your appearance, covering yourself by your variegated pastimes in order to increase others’ prema for you.” They then speak of their good fortune. You have appeared to give good fortune to all people in this world and the next (bhavāya vibhavāya). You have just now appeared because you are the nourisher of all the devotees desiring you (āśiṣām) in your present state (sampratām), when you are performing pastimes in Gokula.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's avatāras are not material bodies but the Supreme Person Himself descending in full potency for our benefit — receive Him personally, not as myth.
    Practical Applications
    • When you read of Kṛṣṇa's childhood pastimes today, refuse the impersonalist reflex to call them symbols — accept them as factual descents of the same Supreme Person.
    • Notice one moment when you reduce Kṛṣṇa to 'one deity among many' or 'the divine within,' and silently correct it: He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
    • Before opening Bhāgavatam or Gītā today, pray for the devotee's eye that sees aśarīriṇaḥ — non-material form — rather than the mūḍha's eye that sees kalpanā.
    Analogy

    A king dressed as a beggar to walk through his city — the beggar's robe is real cloth, the body inside is the king's own. Kṛṣṇa's matsya-form, kūrma-form, varāha-form are not material bodies the way ours are; they are His own person, dressed in fish, tortoise, hog. Aśarīriṇaḥ — not bodied-in-prakṛti.

    Stories
    Varāha and Hiraṇyākṣa

    When Hiraṇyākṣa carried the earth to the cosmic waters, Viṣṇu appeared as a colossal boar — Varāha — and after a long underwater battle slew the demon, lifted the earth on His tusk, and re-established her in orbit.

    A literal hog could not have done any of this. Bhāgavatam (SB 3.13, 3.18–19) emphasizes throughout that the boar-form was aprākṛta-vapus — non-material body, the Supreme Person Himself in boar shape. SB 10.10.34–35 names this principle directly: the avatāra is the same person, not a different creature.

    📝 My note

    Source: vedabase.io

    Important Words
    • parama-kalyāṇa — supremely auspicious
      Compound: parama (supreme) + kalyāṇa (welfare, auspiciousness). Kṛṣṇa is named as the source of all welfare — kalyāṇa-guṇa-rāśi (heap of auspicious qualities) in Gauḍīya formulary. Addressed as the welfare itself, not merely the giver.
    • parama-maṅgala — supremely auspicious
      Compound: parama + maṅgala. Maṅgala specifically connotes ritual auspiciousness, the inauguration of every good thing. Gauḍīya nāma-saṅkīrtana opens with maṅgalācaraṇa precisely because Kṛṣṇa is the maṅgala-source.
    • vāsudevāya — to Vāsudeva, son of Vasudeva
      Dative of Vāsudeva — now read in its other valence: 'son of Vasudeva.' The siddhas address Kṛṣṇa by His family name, acknowledging that this very toddler before them is the same caturvyūha-Vāsudeva of the previous verse. Person, not abstraction.
    • śāntāya — to the most peaceful
      Dative of śānta. Gauḍīya rasa: śānta-rasa is the lowest of the five primary rasas, but śānta as adjective for Bhagavān (His own state) is supreme — undisturbed equipoise even in the midst of līlā. Vraja Kṛṣṇa is śānta and the entire energy-current at once.
    • yadūnām pataye — to the controller of the Yadus
      Genitive plural + dative. Kṛṣṇa is addressed by His relation to His dynasty. Gauḍīya frame: His being Lord of the Yadus is part of His svarūpa, not a temporary social role — Vaikuṇṭha extends Yadu-relations eternally.
    O supremely auspicious, we offer our respectful obeisances unto You, who are the supreme good. O most famous descendant and controller of the Yadu dynasty, O son of Vasudeva, O most peaceful, let us offer our obeisances unto Your lotus feet.
    Purport

    The word parama-kalyāṇa is significant because Kṛṣṇa, in any of His incarnations, appears in order to protect the sādhus ( paritrāṇāya sādhūnām ). The sādhus, saintly persons or devotees, are always harassed by nondevotees, and Kṛṣṇa appears in His incarnations to give them relief. This is His first concern. If we study the history of Kṛṣṇa’s life, we shall find that for most of His life He predominantly engaged in killing demons one after another.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O supremely auspicious, we offer our respectful obeisances unto You, who are the supreme good. O most famous descendant and controller of the Yadu dynasty, O son of Vasudeva, O most peaceful, let us offer our obeisances unto Your lotus feet.
    Commentary

    I pay my respects to you, who gives the greats auspiciousness, prema bhakti, to the jivas (parama kalyana), who is the very form of auspiciousness (parama mangala).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Feeling pleasure in the Lord’s qualities by chanting his names describing those qualities, after indicating that they should get auspiciousness through the Lord’s appearance, unable to serve appropriately, they simply offer respects. O most auspicious form by your very nature (parama-kalyāṇa)! O form which gives auspiciousness or happiness in this and next life to the universe (viśva-maṅgala)! These two phrases indicate devotion with no desires and with desires. Another version has parama-maṅgala—he who is auspicious for Śiva and others. yac-chauca-niḥsṛta-sarit-pravarodakena tīrthena mūrdhny adhikṛtena śivaḥ śivo 'bhūt dhyātur manaḥ-śamala-śaila-nisṛṣṭa-vajraṁ dhyāyec ciraṁ bhagavataś caraṇāravindam One should meditate continually upon the Lord’s lotus feet from which the Gaṅgā flows and gives extra blessings to Śiva on his head, and whose thunderbolt is released upon mountains of sin in the meditator’s mind. SB 3.28.22 How is he auspicious? He appeared through Vasudeva to give benefit to all. He is without fault or with a form of joy (śāntāya). He acts continually as the leader of the Yadu kṣatriyas and the cowherds (yadūdām pataye). Skanda Purāṇa describes the cowherds as Yadus: rakṣītā yādavāḥ sarve indravṛsṭi-nivāraṇāt: he protected all the cowherds (who were Yādavas) from Indra’s rain. Yatrābhiṣikto bhagavān maghonā yadu-vairiṇā: at that place the Lord was bathed by Indra, enemy of the cowherds (Yadus).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having indicates the purpose of the avatāra, they summarize, singing sweet names of unlimited power, while offering respects with devotion. . O most auspicious form by your very nature (parama-kalyāṇa)! Or O person endowed with the highest prema! O form which gives auspiciousness or happiness in this and next life to the universe (viśva-maṅgala)! These two phrases indicate devotion with no desires and with desires. How is he auspicious? He appeared through Vasudeva to give benefit to all. He is without fault or with a form of joy (śāntāya). He acts continually as the leader of the Yadu kṣatriyas and the cowherds (yadūdām pataye). Skanda Purāṇa describes the cowherds as Yadus: rakṣītā yādavāḥ sarve indravṛsṭi-nivāraṇāt: he protected all the cowherds (who were Yādavas) from Indra’s rain. Yatrābhiṣikto bhagavān maghonā yadu-vairiṇā: at that place the Lord was bathed by Indra, enemy of the cowherds (Yadus).

    Or vāsudevāya indicates his birth pastime, śāntāya indicates his lack of anger even in battle and is peaceful, showing dharma when the wives of the brāhmaṇas requested his love. Yadūnām pataye indicates that after going to Mathurā he would perform pastimes in Dvārakā by protecting the Yadus. Thus the goal of all avatāras, expressed by parama-kalyana and viśva-maṅgala, is explained in this summary of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva and Lord of the Yadus, is supremely auspicious and peaceful — bow to Him as the personal shelter who protects His devotees.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin your day by audibly offering praṇāma to Kṛṣṇa as parama-kalyāṇa and parama-maṅgala — name Him personally, not as an abstract Absolute.
    • Notice one situation today where you feel besieged or harassed, and bring it specifically to Vāsudeva as the śānta protector rather than fighting it alone.
    • Refuse to flatten Kṛṣṇa into 'the universe' or 'the divine' — speak His name and lineage (son of Vasudeva, Lord of the Yadus) in at least one prayer today.
    Analogy

    After a long doctrinal exposition, a son turns to his father and simply bows — every argument made was already implicit in the bow. The siddhas have spent verses 29–35 enumerating who Kṛṣṇa is; now they fold their hands and say only namaḥ, four times. Analysis surrenders to namaḥ.

    Important Words
    • anujānīhi — may we have permission
      Imperative second person from anu-√jñā. The freed beings do not assume the right to depart — they ask. Gauḍīya: even mukti does not bypass the protocol of taking permission from guru and Bhagavān; ājñā precedes every step.
    • bhūman — O greatest universal form
      Vocative of bhūman, 'plenitude, vastness.' The siddhas address Kṛṣṇa as the all-pervading vast even while He is a toddler before them. Both seen at once — the privilege of cleansed sight.
    • tava-anucara-kiṅkarau — we are servants of Your most confidential devotee
      Compound: tava (Your) + anucara (intimate associate, Nārada) + kiṅkarau (the two servants). Gauḍīya formula: dāsa-dāsānudāsa. The deepest qualification is to be a servant of a servant — never a direct claimant.
    • anugrahāt — from mercy
      Ablative of anugraha. The verb of the whole chapter — anugraha (SB 10.10.7, 10.10.40) — is now ablative: 'because of the mercy.' The siddhas explicitly name Nārada's mercy as the cause of their seeing Kṛṣṇa. No self-credit anywhere.
    O supreme form, we are always servants of Your servants, especially of Nārada Muni. Now give us permission to leave for our home. It is by the grace and mercy of Nārada Muni that we have been able to see You face to face.
    Purport

    Unless delivered or blessed by a devotee, one cannot realize that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu kaścid yatati siddhaye. According to this verse of Bhagavad-gītā (7.3) , there are so many siddhas or yogīs who cannot understand Kṛṣṇa; instead, they misunderstand Him. But if one takes shelter of a devotee descending from the paramparā system of Nārada ( svayambhūr nāradaḥ śambhuḥ ), one can then understand who is an incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In this age, many pseudo incarnations are advertised simply for having exhibited some magical performances, but except for persons who are servants of Nārada and other servants of Kṛṣṇa, no one can understand who is God and who is not. This is confirmed by Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura. Chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava-sevā nistāra pāyeche kebā: no one is delivered from the material conception of life unless favored by a Vaiṣṇava. Others can never understand, neither by speculation nor by any other bodily or mental gymnastics.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O supreme form, we are always servants of Your servants, especially of Nārada Muni. Now give us permission to leave for our home. It is by the grace and mercy of Nārada Muni that we have been able to see You face to face.
    Commentary

    We are your followers (anucara) and Narada’s servants (kinkarau).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having praised the Lord, thinking it unsuitable to remain there as devatās at an improper time, lamenting their position as trees, they speak. Please permit us to go, O Lord (bhūman)! Or, please give us some instruction, lord perfect in all respects (bhūman). Though you do not need anything, still give us an order to fulfill. Out of affection for the devotees they speak. We are servants of Śiva, your devotee. This was previously stated. Or, we are servants of Nārada, since he by mercy gave us this result. This is reasonable, since it was suitable that they would think of following him. Or, allow us to be servants of your followers at all times. Or, allow us to be servants of your cowherds. Please make us their servants and keep us in that position. “Oh, that is very rare.” We have seen you by the mercy of Nārada, who is most merciful (bhagavataḥ), and has inconceivable prema. We aspire for that since we have attained what is unobtainable, though we were the greatest offenders.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa is realized only through the mercy of His devotee — humbly take shelter of the Vaiṣṇava paramparā as a servant of His servants.
    Practical Applications
    • Identify one living link in the Nārada-paramparā — a guru, sādhu, or devotee — and serve them today in some small, concrete way before asking anything of Kṛṣṇa.
    • Refuse to evaluate Kṛṣṇa or any claimed incarnation by your own speculation; cross-check every spiritual conclusion against what bona fide Vaiṣṇavas in the line of Nārada have said.
    • Speak of yourself today as kiṅkara — servant of the servant — at least once in prayer or conversation, and notice where ahaṅkāra resists the posture.
    Analogy

    A traveler granted audience with the king through his minister's letter — on leaving, the traveler does not thank himself; he carries the minister's name on his lips back into the world. Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva, freed by Kṛṣṇa, name themselves anucara-kiṅkarau — servants of Nārada's servants. The chain of indebtedness is the chain of bhakti.

    Stories
    Caitanya Mahāprabhu and gopī-bhartuḥ-pada-kamalayoḥ dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ

    In the Śikṣāṣṭaka and in the famous verse cited in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Mahāprabhu defines the perfection of bhakti not as 'servant of Kṛṣṇa' but as 'servant of the servant of the servant of the servant of the gopīs' lover.' He compounds dāsa five deep, removing every claim of direct access.

    SB 10.10.37 is one of the scriptural seeds of this teaching. The newly-liberated siddhas do not say 'we are Yours' — they say 'we are servants of Your servant Nārada.' The Gauḍīya door to Kṛṣṇa is always through the Vaiṣṇava.

    Important Words
    • vāṇī — the power of speech
      Nominative of vāṇī. Gauḍīya: speech is the first sense engaged in bhakti — chanting, kīrtana, kathā. Caitanya's siddhānta begins with the tongue (jihva) as both diagnostic and therapeutic organ.
    • guṇa-anukathane — in talking about Your pastimes
      Compound: guṇa (qualities, pastimes) + anukathana (continual telling). Gauḍīya: anu- prefixes indicate the disciple's repetition of what the guru speaks. The siddhas' speech becomes paramparā-anukathana.
    • smṛtyām — in remembrance
      Locative of smṛti — same word from SB 10.10.20–22, where Nārada granted them smṛti during the tree-curse. The smṛti that began as memory of sin now becomes meditation on Kṛṣṇa's feet. Same faculty, redirected.
    • nivāsa-jagat-praṇāme — in obeisance to the whole world as Your dwelling
      Compound: nivāsa (dwelling) + jagat (world) + praṇāma (obeisance). Gauḍīya acintya-bhedābheda in one phrase: the world is His dwelling — non-different in being His energy, different in not being Him personally. The head bows to the world as His vyakta-rūpa.
    • bhavat-tanūnām — who are nondifferent from You
      Compound: bhavat (Your) + tanu (body). Vaiṣṇavas are addressed as 'Your own bodies.' Gauḍīya: vaiṣṇava-aparādha is the gravest offense precisely because the devotee is Kṛṣṇa's tanu. The eyes that see Vaiṣṇavas see Kṛṣṇa Himself.
    Henceforward, may all our words describe Your pastimes, may our ears engage in aural reception of Your glories, may our hands, legs and other senses engage in actions pleasing to You, and may our minds always think of Your lotus feet. May our heads offer our obeisances to everything within this world, because all things are also Your different forms, and may our eyes see the forms of Vaiṣṇavas, who are nondifferent from You.
    Purport

    Here the process of understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead is given. This process is bhakti. śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ sakhyam ātma-nivedanam ( Bhāg. 7.5.23) Everything should be engaged in the service of the Lord. Hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate ( Nārada-pañcarātra ). Everything — the mind, the body and all the sense organs — should be engaged in Kṛṣṇa’s service. This is to be learned from expert devotees like Nārada, Svayambhū and Śambhu. This is the process. We cannot manufacture our own way of understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for it is not that everything one manufactures or concocts will lead to understanding God. Such a proposition — yata mata, tata patha — is foolish. Kṛṣṇa says, bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ: “Only by executing the activities of bhakti can one understand Me.” ( Bhāg. 11.14.21 ) This is called ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanam, remaining engaged favorably in the service of the Lord.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Henceforward, may all our words describe Your pastimes, may our ears engage in aural reception of Your glories, may our hands, legs and other senses engage in actions pleasing to You, and may our minds always think of Your lotus feet. May our heads offer our obeisances to everything within this world, because all things are also Your different forms, and may our eyes see the forms of Vaiṣṇavas, who are nondifferent from You.
    Commentary

    As we are your followers and Narada’s servants, you should be very merciful to us. We now pray form something rarely given to others. The particle ca should be understood after each item. May our words (vani) always be engaged in describing your qualities (guna kathane), and nothing else (ca). may our minds be engaged in remembering your lotus feet. May our heads pay respects to the living entities (jagat), the devotees such as Narada. Or nivasa jagat can be a vocative, o abode of the universe (jagat nivasa), may our eyes be engaged in seeing your forms (bhavat tanuman) and those of your devotees such as Narada (satam).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “Since Nārada made you devotees, go to him.” Then give us all the methods of bhakti. They pray in this way, which is the nature of bhakti. May our words or voice speak continuously of the qualities of your feet, of your affection for your devotees and of your beauty-- not about yoga or sacrifices. May our minds be thinking of your feet, with devotion-- not just thinking. May our two ears be engaged in hearing topics about you with full attention (with two ears). Similarly both hands should engage in action for you fully. Let us hear all topics—including how you enable Brahmā to carry out creation. Since the ears are not completely independent of what they hear, at least in speaking, we should speak only about the sweet qualities of the Lord because of their rasa. The hands and other organs (ca) should be engaged in actions like deity worship and related services. The head should offer respects to you, O dweller in the universe! Śiras is mentioned last since this is the main limb of the body. The word tava is repeated to indicate that by offering respects to the Lord respects are offered to the world, since the Lord is everything, and thus perfection in offering respects is achieved, Or may our heads offer respects to the Vaiṣṇavas, the living beings (jagat) who are your dwelling place, for it is said śiras tu tasyobhaya-liṅgam ānamet: an actual head is one that bows down to the Lord in his manifestations among the moving and nonmoving creatures. (SB 10.80.4) Or may our heads offer respects to the people of Vraja where you dwell, even though they are far away for us. May our eyes see devotees like Nārada who are your body. Or may our eyes directly see you in your deity forms and the devotees. However to see him directly in their house was impossible. Out of fear they did not pray for this. Touching and smelling are also understood though not mentioned in the verse.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “Since Nārada made you devotees, go to him.” Then give us all the methods of bhakti. They pray in this way, which is the nature of bhakti. Or having attained closeness to Vāsudeva, we ask you for another mercy. Let us be devotees and supply other things as well. May our words or voice speak continuously of the qualities of your feet, of your affection for your devotees and of your beauty-- not about yoga or sacrifices. Mention of the feet indicates desire for service. Dry jṣāna is discarded. May our two ears be engaged in hearing topics about you with full attention (with two ears). They speak in the plural (naḥ), thinking of blessings for their relatives as well. The ears should hear your topics and not act independently. Because of qualification for describing the Lord’s glories, they mention guṇānu-kathana. The hands and other organs (ca) should be engaged in actions like deity worship and related services. The head should offer respects to you, O dweller in the universe! Śiras is mentioned last since this is the main limb of the body and is used in offering respects with eight limbs. Other limbs should also be included when mention is made of the head. Or it is not possible to offer respects with just the head, and one engages the hands and other limbs when serving the Lord, even when doing kīrtana once. O lord who lives within the universe (nivāsa-jagat). The word tava is repeated to indicate that by offering respects to the Lord respects are offered to the world, since the Lord is everything, and thus perfection in offering respects is achieved. Our eyes should be engaged in seeking devotees, in which you always manifest yourself or our eyes should see the devotees within whom forms of the Lord like śālagrāmas are worshipped. Or our eyes should see the devotees and the forms of the Lord. They do not pray that the Lord directly appear in their homes out of fear. In this way six types of bhakti are mentioned: kīrtana, śvaraṇa, pūjā, paricaryā, smaraṇa and vandana. Sakhya and ātma-nivedana are generally included in the goal (sādhya) and are thus not mentioned in a prayer about sādhana. Or these two are naturally the result of the other six. Or the two are included in smaraṇa, being particular bhāvas. Karmārpaṇa and dāsya is included in kīrtana and other processes. Normally speaking words agitate all the senses. They pray for kīrtana because by doing that the other senses become happily engaged in their respective actions. Or kīrtana is the main process because the Lord prefers it. Nāhaṁ vasāmi vaikuṇṭhe: I do not reside in Vaikuṇṭha. Or kīrtana produces a special rasa. Seeing the devotees and deities is the same as seeing the Lord directly. Since seeing the Lord directly is the end result of all processes of bhakti, this is mentioned last. The other processes mentioned in the middle one can do according to one’s taste.

      His Holiness Radha Govinda Swami· 2012-10-28· English
    Personal Guidance
    Engage every sense — speech, hearing, hands, mind, head, eyes — in Kṛṣṇa's service; bhakti is the only authentic process to know Him.
    Practical Applications
    • Audit one sense today (tongue, ears, or eyes) and redirect it from viṣaya to a concrete act of bhakti — speak of His pastimes, hear a kīrtana, behold a Vaiṣṇava.
    • Refuse the yata mata, tata patha attitude in your own life: drop one self-invented 'spiritual practice' and replace it with a śāstra-given limb of bhakti — śravaṇa, kīrtana, or smaraṇa.
    • Before sleep tonight, offer praṇāma with your head to the Vaiṣṇavas you encountered, recognizing each as bhavat-tanu — His own form.
    Analogy

    A whole orchestra dedicated to one melody — the speaker on speech, the hearer on hearing, the hands on rhythm, the mind on the absent beat, the eyes on the conductor. The siddhas pledge every sense to Kṛṣṇa's līlā by name: vāṇī to His pastimes, śravaṇau to His kathā, hastau to His mission, manas to His feet, śiras to praṇāma, dṛṣṭi to His Vaiṣṇavas. Each instrument is given its part.

    Stories
    Hanumān's six-sense surrender

    Hanumān, asked how he had crossed the ocean and burned Laṅkā, replied that his speech was Rāma's name, his hearing Rāma's glories, his hands Rāma's work, his mind Rāma's feet, his head Rāma's praṇāma, and his eyes Rāma's form. Every sense had a single destination.

    SB 10.10.38 enumerates the same pledge in the same form, sense by sense. The verse becomes the template for the morning prayer of the Vaiṣṇava: pañca-indriya samarpaṇa as the entry-fee of the day.

    Important Words
    • gokula-īśvaraḥ — the master of Gokula
      Compound: Gokula + īśvara. Kṛṣṇa is Lord even in His most intimate Vraja-līlā. Gauḍīya: aiśvarya and mādhurya coexist; the gopīs feel mādhurya predominantly, but the title īśvara is never relinquished.
    • dāmnā — by the rope
      Instrumental of dāman, 'rope.' The source of the name Dāmodara. The rope is a piece of household twine; the bound one is the cause of all causes. Gauḍīya: this is the supreme image of Kṛṣṇa being controlled by His devotee's love.
    • baddhaḥ — bound
      Past participle from √bandh. The same word used for the conditioned soul's bondage — turned upside down. The Lord of bondage is the bound One; the rope-binder is the devotee. Mādhurya inverts the cosmology.
    • prahasan — smiling
      Present participle from pra-√has, 'to smile widely.' Kṛṣṇa smiles because the binding is His own play. Gauḍīya: every līlā has hāsya as undertone in mādhurya — the Lord's delight in being constrained by His devotee's affection.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: The two young demigods thus offered prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Godhead, is the master of all and was certainly Gokuleśvara, the master of Gokula, He was bound to the wooden mortar by the ropes of the gopīs, and therefore, smiling widely, He spoke to the sons of Kuvera the following words.
    Purport

    Kṛṣṇa was smiling because He was thinking to Himself, “These two young demigods fell from the higher planetary system to this planet, and I have delivered them from the bondage of standing for a long time as trees, but as for Me, I am bound by the ropes of the gopīs and am subject to their chastisements.” In other words, Kṛṣṇa submits to being chastised and bound by the gopīs because of pure love and affection worthy of being praised by a devotee in so many ways.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: The two young demigods thus offered prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Godhead, is the master of all and was certainly Gokuleśvara, the master of Gokula, He was bound to the wooden mortar by the ropes of the gopīs, and therefore, smiling widely, He spoke to the sons of Kuvera the following words.
    Commentary

    Sankirtitah means completely glorified. Damna ca hints at being bound not only by ropes, but by prema also. Prahasan means that he smiled very sweetly, thinking these two minor devatas have been bound up by his maya. "They are praising me for freeing them from this bondage. But mother Yasoda binds me up and scolds me instead of praising me. Still out of love I stay in Gokula. The love I have for the scolding by the inhabitants of Vraja is much more than the praises I receive from these sons of Kuvera."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Laughing, the lord of Gokula spoke to the two sons of Kuvera. Referring to their previous state, the Lord showed their great fortune. He smiled because, though he was glorified by the two as the Lord, he was still bound to the mortar by a rope. First of all he was bound. But he was bound by a mere rope, and to a mortar among all things! The two in fear did not laugh. Seeing them in that condition he laughed. He rules over Gokula and as the cause of our good fortune (bhagavān) is eternally performing pastimes in Gokula because of being controlled by the prema of his devotees. Gokula should be understood to have the highest qualities.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though he was lord of Gokula, and was bound to the mortar, because he was affectionate to the devotees, he spoke to the two. Or though he was absorbed in playing in Gokula (ca), he spoke to them. Or though giving mercy solely to the people of Gokula, and though bound by the mortar, he spoke to them, because he appeared to give benefit to all people (bhagavān). Or as lord of Gokula, taking birth there, it was proper to speak even to the two, because he was controlled by the people of Gokula, even (ca) being tied up by them. He did not even free himself, because he was having fun playing in Gokula (gokuleśvaraḥ). He was moreover the essence of all unlimited powers. By the mercy of Nārada the two were most fortunate. His laugh was natural. Or he laughed because of the mercy of Nārada on their previous condition. Or he laughed in joy on hearing their praises. Or he laughed in amusement, on showing himself bound up. He was not being deceptive in laughing. Another meaning is he is lord of all the senses (gokuleśvaraḥ). By his power, he can give bhakti to all the senses. Thus the prayer of the two would be fulfilled.

      His Holiness Romapada Swami· 2019-01-15· English
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa, master of Gokula, lets Himself be bound by the gopīs' ropes — pure love conquers the Lord whom no power can bind.
    Practical Applications
    • Notice today where you try to 'control' Kṛṣṇa through bargaining or demand, and instead offer one act of simple, ropelike affection — a chant, a prayer, a service done without leverage.
    • Speak to someone you love with the bhāva of a gopī — small, tender, unselfconscious — rather than with the calculation of a worshipper seeking returns.
    • Refuse to reduce Kṛṣṇa to an impersonal Absolute today; address Him by name in your sādhana as Gokuleśvara, the personal Lord who submits to His devotees' love.
    Analogy

    A young king ties up his own father's hand in a game of dice and the father lets him — the strength of the bound man is far greater than the rope, but the rope is held by his beloved, and so it holds. Kṛṣṇa is Gokuleśvara, Lord of all Gokula — and He is bound to a mortar by Yaśodā's rope. Love's geometry: the supreme is constrained by the small, because He chooses to be.

    Stories
    Yaśodā's rope and the two-finger excess

    Yaśodā tried to bind the naughty Kṛṣṇa to the mortar; her rope fell two fingers short. She added another, and another — every rope was always two fingers short. SB 10.9 records this exquisitely.

    Finally, seeing her exhaustion, Kṛṣṇa allowed Himself to be bound. The 'two fingers' Gauḍīya ācāryas read as vidhi and bhāva — both are needed; rules alone never reach Him, but rules paired with the gopī's love do. SB 10.10.39 closes the curtain on this scene: the Lord of Gokula speaks while bound, smiling — because the bondage is His own choice and His own pleasure.

    Important Words
    • karuṇā-ātmanā — by one whose nature is compassion
      Compound: karuṇā (compassion) + ātmā (self). Nārada is named as 'one whose very self is compassion.' Gauḍīya: a Vaiṣṇava's anger and curse are subroutines of his compassion — never independent emotions.
    • śrī-mada-andhayoḥ — of those blinded by intoxication of wealth
      Dual genitive of compound used for them in SB 10.10.7. The chapter closes the diagnosis with the same words it opened — confirming that the disease was correctly named throughout, and the medicine fit the disease.
    • vāgbhiḥ — by words (the curse)
      Instrumental plural of vāc. Nārada's instrument was speech — vāc, the same faculty SB 10.10.38 will dedicate to Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. The same instrument: in Nārada's mouth it cursed; in the devotee's mouth it praises. Vāc is direction-of-bhāva, not substance.
    • anugrahaḥ — favor, special mercy
      Nominative of anugraha — the chapter's hinge word, appearing in SB 10.10.7 (Nārada's intention) and SB 10.10.37 (the siddhas' acknowledgment) and now SB 10.10.40 (Kṛṣṇa's confirmation). Three appearances trace the arc — intention, recognition, ratification.
    The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: The great saint Nārada Muni is very merciful. By his curse, he showed the greatest favor to both of you, who were mad after material opulence and who had thus become blind. Although you fell from the higher planet Svargaloka and became trees, you were most favored by him. I knew of all these incidents from the very beginning.
    Purport

    It is now confirmed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead that the curse of a devotee is also to be regarded as mercy. As Kṛṣṇa, God, is all-good, a Vaiṣṇava is also all-good. Whatever he does is good for everyone. This is explained in the following verse.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: The great saint Nārada Muni is very merciful. By his curse, he showed the greatest favor to both of you, who were mad after material opulence and who had thus become blind. Although you fell from the higher planet Svargaloka and became trees, you were most favored by him. I knew of all these incidents from the very beginning.
    Commentary

    Narada gave mercy in the form of destroying their opulence through his instructions starting with verse 8 nahy anyo jusato josyan.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I have known about this incident (Nārada’s arrangement). Otherwise it would not be suitable for me to show mercy to great offenders. Or pleased that they recognized that their condition was Nārada’s mercy, to confirm their conclusion, he agreed with them in order to give the two joy. For this reason he makes the statement. Nārada was most merciful (karuṇātmanā), and thus he gave mercy to the two even though they were drunkards. Or, Nārada showed mercy by his words of benediction (vāgbhiḥ). Nārada had said “I will take away your wealth so that you will not act in this way again.” By these words, they fell into darkness (vigata-bhramśaḥ), into hellish existence because of great offense. Or by his words they became sober, devoid of illusion (vigata-bhraṁśaḥ) by attaining closeness to the Lord’s pastimes in Gokula and attaining the highest bhakti.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa Himself confirms: a Vaiṣṇava's curse is mercy in disguise — wealth-blindness is the real fall, his correction the real anugraha.
    Practical Applications
    • Notice today where śrī-mada — pride in opulence, status, or success — is quietly blinding you, and name one specific area where it has shut your eyes.
    • When a devotee or guru-figure says something that stings, refuse the reflex to defend yourself; sit with it for ten minutes as possible anugraha before responding.
    • Identify one comfort or possession you treat as proof of your worth, and offer it mentally to Kṛṣṇa today, asking Him to remove its grip before it has to be removed by force.
    Analogy

    A surgeon, having lanced the abscess, confirms to the patient: 'That hurt, and it was meant to. You were poisoning yourself; he drained the wound.' Kṛṣṇa Himself ratifies Nārada's curse here — calling it karuṇā, anugraha — closing the case the chapter opened with Parīkṣit's diagnostic question. Diagnosis to surgery to confirmation.

    Stories
    Kuntī's prayer for calamities

    After the war, Kuntī Devi prayed before Kṛṣṇa: vipadaḥ santu naḥ śaśvat tatra tatra jagad-guro / bhavato darśanaṁ yat syād apunar bhava-darśanam — 'Let calamities befall us again and again, for in them we see You.'

    SB 1.8.25 makes explicit what SB 10.10.40 confirms: the apparent reverse is anugraha because it carries remembrance of Bhagavān with it. Kṛṣṇa's own validation of Nārada's curse uses the same logic — vibhraṁśa (the fall to tree-form) was anugraha-kṛta. The Vaiṣṇava reads every fall this way.

    Important Words
    • sādhūnām — of devotees
      Genitive plural of sādhu — same word used in SB 10.10.17 and 10.10.18 for those who associate freely with the poor. The chapter has trained the reader's ear: by now sādhu means 'one who has accomplished bhakti,' nothing less.
    • sama-cittānām — of those who are equally disposed toward everyone
      Compound: sama (equal) + citta (consciousness). Same compound used in SB 10.10.18. Gauḍīya: equal-vision (sama-darśana, sama-citta) is the sādhu's automatic posture, because every jīva is seen as Kṛṣṇa's part.
    • mat-kṛta-ātmanām — of those who are fully surrendered to Me
      Compound: mat (Me) + kṛta (made, dedicated) + ātmā (self). 'Whose very self has been made over to Me.' Gauḍīya: this is ātma-nivedana, the sixth and final aṅga of nine-fold bhakti; it is also the second-last of the six aṅgas of śaraṇāgati.
    • darśanāt — simply by seeing
      Ablative of darśana — same root as the rūpa-darśana of SB 10.10.20–22's prophecy. The whole chapter is bookended by darśana: the curse promised it, the chapter delivers it, and now Kṛṣṇa Himself names darśana as the sufficient cause.
    • savituḥ — of the sun
      Genitive of savitṛ — the sun, especially the morning sun. Same word in the Gāyatrī. The sādhu is compared to savitṛ — light-giver, ignorance-dispeller — and the comparison is exact, not metaphorical: both reveal what was always there once the eye is turned toward them.
    When one is face to face with the sun, there is no longer darkness for one’s eyes. Similarly, when one is face to face with a sādhu, a devotee, who is fully determined and surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one will no longer be subject to material bondage.
    Purport

    As stated by Caitanya Mahāprabhu (Cc. Madhya 22.54): ‘sādhu-saṅga,’ ‘sādhu-saṅga’ — sarva-śāstre kaya lava-mātra sādhu-saṅge sarva-siddhi haya If by chance one meets a sādhu, a devotee, one’s life is immediately successful, and one is freed from material bondage. It may be argued that whereas someone may receive a sādhu with great respect, someone else may not receive a sādhu with such respect. A sādhu, however, is always equipoised toward everyone. Because of being a pure devotee, a sādhu is always ready to deliver Kṛṣṇa consciousness without discrimination. As soon as one sees a sādhu, one naturally becomes free. Nonetheless, persons who are too much offensive, who commit vaiṣṇava-aparādhas, or offenses to a sādhu, will have to take some time before being rectified. This is also indicated herein.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    When one is face to face with the sun, there is no longer darkness for one's eyes. Similarly, when one is face to face with a sādhu, a devotee, who is fully determined and surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one will no longer be subject to material bondage.
    Commentary

    Since, on seeing Narada, you disrespected him, how is it possible that he could give mercy to you? This verse answers the question. From seeing those whose minds are not disturbed by respect or disrespect ( sama cittanam) who have offered their minds completely to me (sutaram matkrt atmanam), one is released from bondage. Instead of darsanat na there is another reading darsan antah. In that case the meaning would be just until one takes darsana of the devotee, bondage will remain. Just as the sun destroys darkness just by its rising, , so just up to seeing the devotee, bondage remains, by seeing him it is destroyed. It should be understood from this example however that though the sun rises, if a person is blind, the darkness is not dissipated. In the same way, if there is nama aparadha, as in the case of the asuras, even seeing Narada will not release them from bondage.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Taking the meaning of the first line from Śrīdhara Svāmī, by seeing those who follow proper conduct (sādhūnām) or who realize ātmā (sama-cittānām), bondage is somewhat reduced. More than this (sutarām), by seeing those who are constantly thinking of me, bondage is completely removed, since they have the greatest mercy. Or, the devotees are most merciful (sādhūnām) and they do not take offense seriously (sama-cittānām). Because they are constantly devoted to me (mat-kṛtātmanām), the other two qualities naturally follow. Seeing them, no human being has bondage to saṁsāra. What to speak of the devotees talking to them. And what to speak of you two being great offenders. Sutarām indicates that this effect does not take place by hearing and chanting to the extent that it does by seeing devotees. The eyes are relieved of darkness to a high degree from (sutarām) on seeing the sun. This indicates that even previous to seeing the sun, darkness is removed.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Just by seeing devotees, any person becomes free of material bondage. So what is the need of you two asking for mercy by uttering so many words? Any human (puṁsaḥ) is qualified to see the devotee. Though before seeing the sun, darkness is destroyed and the eyes can see to some degree, by seeing devotees, saṁsāra is completely destroyed.

    Personal Guidance
    Stand before a sādhu fixed in Kṛṣṇa as you would face the sun — the darkness of material bondage simply cannot remain.
    Practical Applications
    • Seek out one sādhu-saṅga today — in person, through Prabhupāda's recorded class, or by reading a pure devotee's words — and approach without reservation.
    • Refuse the calculation of whether the sādhu 'likes you back'; he is sama-citta, so receive his mercy without demanding personal recognition.
    • Notice and immediately correct any tendency to criticize or measure a devotee, guarding strictly against vaiṣṇava-aparādha that would delay your freedom.
    Analogy

    When the sun rises over the eastern peak, the question is not whether the cave is dark — the question is whether it has an opening. Stand before a sādhu fixed in Kṛṣṇa, and the darkness simply cannot remain; what is required is not the cave's own brightness but its turning toward the sun. Darśana is the opening.

    Stories
    Caitanya Mahāprabhu at Govardhana

    When Mahāprabhu came to Vraja and walked around Govardhana, the simple cowherds, jungle-dwellers, and unlettered villagers who saw Him became, in that one darśana, prema-bhaktas. He did not give them mantras or instruction; the sight of His form was sufficient.

    SB 10.10.41 names the principle Kṛṣṇa Himself enunciates: a sādhu fixed in Bhagavān (mat-kṛta-ātmā) is to be seen, and the seeing is the means. Caitanya-līlā is the verse's living demonstration in Kali-yuga.

    Important Words
    • mat-paramau — accepting Me as the supreme destination
      Compound: mat + parama. The Gītā term mat-paraḥ (Gītā 6.47) made dual for the two brothers. Gauḍīya: parama-niṣṭhā (fixed exclusive determination) on Kṛṣṇa is the qualification that secures against fall.
    • bhāvaḥ — devotional ecstasy / sentiment
      Nominative of bhāva. In Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, bhāva is the stage between sādhana and prema — the dawn of pure devotional sentiment. Kṛṣṇa names exactly this stage as already saturated (sañjāta) in them.
    • īpsitaḥ — desired
      Past participle from desid. of √āp — 'desired, hankered for.' Bhakti begins when the jīva himself begins to want it. Gauḍīya: Kṛṣṇa does not impose bhakti; He grants it where the īpsā (sincere desire) has arisen. The brothers' desire is named first, then confirmed.
    • abhavaḥ — freedom from material existence
      From a- + bhava — 'no-becoming.' The end of saṁsāra. Paired with paramaḥ (the highest) — this is the highest abhava: liberation expressed as eternal sevā, not as merging. Gauḍīya distinction: abhava here is liberation-in-bhakti, not śūnyatā.
    O Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva, now you may both return home. Since you desire to be always absorbed in My devotional service, your desire to develop love and affection for Me will be fulfilled, and now you will never fall from that platform.
    Purport

    The highest perfection of life is to come to the platform of devotional service and always engage in devotional activities. Understanding this, Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva desired to attain that platform, and the Supreme Personality of Godhead blessed them with the fulfillment of their transcendental desire.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva, now you may both return home. Since you desire to be always absorbed in My devotional service, your desire to develop love and affection for Me will be fulfilled, and now you will never fall from that platform.
    Commentary

    Though the two brothers were there, he spoke to the chief one , "O Nalakuvara! You who take me as supremely worthy of service, go to your home (sadanam), because that will not bring about bondage any longer (abhava)."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    You are fully surrendered to me because you have developed love for me. You have developed prema (paramaḥ). There is no material existence (abhavaḥ) for you. This is Śrīdhara Svāmī’s explanation. Or by Nārada’ mercy you have strongly (sam) developed prema for me because you desired the highest manifestation (paramaḥ bhavaḥ), pure bhakti described in verse 36. Because Nārada was completely satisfied, since Nārada’s mercy had been involved, the Lord would be satisfied as well. Because the Lord is the ocean of natural, sweet qualities such as humility, he does not speak of having given them direct association.

    Personal Guidance
    When you sincerely desire constant devotional service to Kṛṣṇa, He Himself secures that desire — return to your duties without fear of falling.
    Practical Applications
    • Name out loud, in your morning prayer today, the one desire you actually want Kṛṣṇa to fulfill — and let it be bhakti, not a material outcome.
    • Return to your 'home' — your prescribed duties, family, and sādhana — instead of romanticizing escape; serve Kṛṣṇa from exactly where He has placed you.
    • Refuse the anxiety of falling from devotional service: when sincere desire for bhakti is set, trust His promise and keep chanting and serving today.
    Analogy

    A king, having quietly secured his ministers' loyalty, releases them back to their provinces — they will not betray him now, because the bond is from inside, not from court watchfulness. Kṛṣṇa releases Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva to their celestial home with the seal: their desire for sevā is now sañjāta, fully grown — they cannot fall.

    Stories
    Dhruva's return

    After Viṣṇu appeared to him, Dhruva did not stay in samādhi or seek immediate dissolution. He returned home, became king, ruled justly for thirty-six thousand years, then took to the forest at the end — and finally to Vaikuṇṭha. His desire for Bhagavān, once kindled, did not require him to abandon his post.

    SB 10.10.42 grants Nalakūvara and Maṇigrīva the same trajectory: 'go home now.' Once the bhāva is sañjāta, the celestial planet is just one more stop on the way to Vaikuṇṭha — there is no falldown from a desire Kṛṣṇa Himself has confirmed.

    Word-for-word
